original_value: The control of the main environmental factors that influence the quality of perishable products is one of the main challenges of the food industry. Temperature is the main factor affecting quality, but other factors like relative humidity and gas concentrations (mainly C2H4, O2 and CO2) also play an important role in maintaining the postharvest quality of horticultural products. For this reason, monitoring such environmental factors is a key procedure to assure quality throughout shelf life and evaluate losses. Therefore, in order to estimate the quality losses that a perishable product can suffer during storage and transportation, a real-time monitoring system has been developed. This system can be used in all post-harvest steps thanks to its Wi-Fi wireless communication architecture. Several laboratory trials were conducted, using lettuce as a model, to determine quality-rating scales during shelf life under different storage temperature conditions. As a result, a multiple non-linear regression (MNLR) model is proposed relating the temperature and the maximum shelf life. This proposed model would allow to predict the days the commodities will reduce their theoretical shelf-life when an improper temperature during storage or in-transit occurs. The system, developed as a sensor-based tool, has been tested during several land transportation trips around Europe.

result.paraphrase: Controlling the main environmental factors that affect the quality of perishable goods is a major challenge for the food industry. Although temperature is the primary determinant of quality, other variables such as relative humidity and gas concentrations—mainly C2H4, O2, and CO2—also significantly influence the postharvest quality of horticultural products. Monitoring these conditions is therefore essential for preserving quality throughout shelf life and assessing losses. To estimate the quality degradation a perishable product may experience during storage and transport, a real-time monitoring system was developed. Thanks to its Wi-Fi wireless communication architecture, the system can be used across all postharvest stages. Using lettuce as a model, several laboratory trials were carried out to establish quality-rating scales during shelf life under different storage temperatures. The outcome is a proposed multiple non-linear regression (MNLR) model linking temperature with maximum shelf life. This model would make it possible to predict how many days commodities will lose from their theoretical shelf life when unsuitable storage or in-transit temperatures occur. Developed as a sensor-based tool, the system has been tested in several land transportation trips across Europe.
